on CI's macOS runners: whether launchd starts a killed guardian again, after what delay, and in the same coalition;
    - **Run on CI** (probe P-8, 2026-10-28): after `kill -9`, launchd started the guardian again 50 ms later when it had run 12 seconds, and 10 seconds later when it had run under 10 seconds (launchd's default `ThrottleInterval`), in the same resource and jetsam coalitions, and ended the killed guardian's child. A guardian started again that removed its own job with `launchctl bootout` ended itself and its child, and launchd didn't start it again in the next 20 seconds. So PO-16's macOS backstop works. **Not tested:** on a stock Mac; CI's macOS runners have SIP turned off (D-34), which shouldn't change what launchd does.
